title: Is the TI LP-MSPM0G3507 the right board for my project?
short: TI's LaunchPad for the MSPM0G3507 chip: an 80 MHz Arm Cortex-M0+ with 128 kB of flash, 32 kB of RAM, a math accelerator and the debugger on the board. It blinked in 2 min 29 s from board in hand with the tools installed, drove a 3.5 inch touch screen, and ran edge AI models and Zephyr. It has no radio, and 32 kB of RAM and 128 kB of flash are what limit bigger programs.

meet.what: A LaunchPad development kit for TI's MSPM0G3507 microcontroller. A USB debugger and serial port are built in, so one cable powers it, programs it and carries its text output. It has a red LED, an RGB LED, two buttons, a thermistor, a light sensor and 40-pin BoosterPack headers for plug-on boards.
facts: Two 12-bit 4 Msps ADCs, a 12-bit DAC, 2 op-amps, 3 comparators, a math accelerator (divide, square root, multiply-accumulate, trig), AES, CAN-FD, 4 UARTs, 2 I2C, 2 SPI
TI MSPM0 SDK 2.11 (DriverLib and TI Drivers) and upstream Zephyr (board lp_mspm0g3507)
$20.56 at TI.com (2026-10-09); stock shows only after a login

projects.t: Blink an LED with TI's SDK
projects.result: 2 min 29 s from board in hand to our own changed blink, tools already installed; CCStudio build 6 s
3 min to blinking from a clean machine with our setup script (about 9.5 min the first time, with a workaround found on the way)

projects.t: Show text on a small screen
projects.result: Full-screen fill 67 ms at 40 MHz SPI, 365 ms at 8 MHz; 64 of 64 pixels of one row read back right at every speed
10 of 10 stored digits right; 34 ms per digit at 80 MHz
Room-occupancy models of 500 to 30k weights: 4.0 to 129 ms per answer at 80 MHz, 20 of 20 right

projects.t: Dim an LED or move a servo
projects.result: TI's PWM examples run, and their output was not measured; a ported PWM program read 14.7% high against 12.5% duty on one channel
Four Arduino programs built and two ran on our API layer; no Arduino core for MSPM0 found

chains.t: TI's MSPM0 SDK, DriverLib, no operating system
chains.why: 262 of 270 TI examples build from a terminal, and every one that was safe to run ran with no crash (213 flashed and run)
Blinky runs. A blinky-class app uses 12,704 bytes of flash and 3,992 bytes of RAM; CoreMark under Zephyr scores 95 to 140 depending on compiler flags

chains.verdict: Builds with this repo's script; not run
chains.why: TI's 48 MSPM0 FreeRTOS example makefiles fail as shipped. Our build script builds TI Drivers on FreeRTOS for this board: 21,040 bytes of flash and 7,059 bytes of RAM

chains.t: Bluetooth host on the chip, radio on another chip over UART
chains.why: Zephyr's Bluetooth host with H4 over UART builds for this board: a beacon needs 39,256 bytes of flash and 14,592 bytes of RAM, the heart-rate peripheral sample 98,600 and 22,164. The radio end of the wire was not built here

chains.t: Thread host (OpenThread) for a separate radio
chains.why: TI's CC1354P10 host build needs 467,648 bytes of flash and 128,916 bytes of RAM against this chip's 131,072 and 32,768

Working memory; this is what runs out first

good_for: A first board: the debugger is on it, and the blink took 2 min 29 s with the tools installed
Screens: a 3.5 inch touch display on 12 jumper wires, 67 ms for a full-screen fill and LVGL in 25.1 kB of RAM
Edge AI models in plain C: occupancy models of up to 30k weights ran, and a handwritten-digit net reads a digit in 34 ms
Zephyr on a board upstream Zephyr already supports
Control maths with a speed-up: a math accelerator gives one motor-control step in 88.5 µs against 172 µs without it, and 70.8 kHz in IQmath fixed point
not_for: Anything with a radio: the chip has none; a separate radio chip can sit on a UART or SPI link
Programs over about 128 kB: the chip has no external memory bus, and the trimmed LVGL demo already uses 125.4 kB
Floating-point control loops at tens of kHz: there is no floating-point unit, so a float motor-control step cannot run at 50 kHz
A Thread or Matter host on the chip: TI's Thread host build is about 94 kB of RAM short
Bluetooth or Wi-Fi without a second chip

instead.why: 512 kB of flash and 128 kB of RAM

a Cortex-M33 with a floating-point unit; one control step in 117 cycles (0.585 µs) with its trig unit and 656 cycles (3.28 µs) in plain software at 200 MHz; the whole trigger, ADC, step and PWM-write loop takes 1.33 µs against 4.74 µs
the board TI's Thread and Matter software targets
the lowest-priced radio board in the catalog ($27.50); it needs the separate $59.29 LP-XDS110ET probe

buy: $20.56 at TI.com for one board (2026-10-09); stock shows only after a login. The debug probe is on the board, so one USB cable does power, flashing and the serial port.
gotchas: your serial window goes silent after you moved jumpers J21 and J22 for the UART loopback
move J21 and J22 back up to XDS (mspm0g3507/example-sweep/JUMPERS.md)
the screen stays dark or shows static although every wire is right
wait about 10 µs after chip select goes high before the next command; the second of two back-to-back commands is lost (mspm0g3507/FAQ.md)
the touch chip does not answer on I2C1 at address 0x38
drive the two pins as software I2C; it answered every time that way (mspm0g3507/display-test/README.md)
your SysConfig clock line is ignored and the chip stays at 32 MHz when you ask for 80
remove SYSCTL.forceDefaultClkConfig and set the clocks through the clock tree (mspm0g3507/FAQ.md)
16-bit SPI frames are silently ignored and the picture is garbled
switch the SPI block off, set the frame size, then switch it back on (mspm0g3507/FAQ.md)
a ported button interrupt never fires on S1
S1 (PA18) is active-high on this board; set PA18 to pull-down with a rising-edge interrupt in SysConfig (mspm0g3507/FAQ.md)
a ported ADC program converts once and then stalls
set the DMA sample count to 1 and point the DMA at the ADC result registers, not the FIFO address (mspm0g3507/FAQ.md)
`make` in `Debug/` stops with `invalid option -- O`
use the gmake that ships with CCStudio, at ccs/utils/bin/gmake (mspm0g3507/FAQ.md)
OpenOCD's `program ... verify` fails about every other time
run it again; the next attempt passes (mspm0g3507/FAQ.md)
the Mac sees nothing when you plug the board in
try another micro-USB cable; a charge-only cable looks the same (mspm0g3507/STOPWATCH.md)
measured_on: Measured 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-09 on an Intel Mac (macOS 15.7) with CCStudio 21.0.1, MSPM0 SDK 2.11.00.07, SysConfig 1.26.3 to 1.28.1 and TI Arm Clang 5.1.1; Zephyr 4.4.2 with GCC 12.2.

hotspots.label: The chip
hotspots.title: MSPM0G3507
hotspots.text: An 80 MHz Arm Cortex-M0+ with 128 kB of flash and 32 kB of RAM. What sets it apart: a math accelerator for divide, square root and trig, two 4 Msps ADCs and CAN-FD.

hotspots.label: Built-in debug probe
hotspots.title: XDS110 probe
hotspots.text: The right half of the board is the debugger. One USB cable powers the board, flashes it and carries its text output, with no separate probe to buy.

hotspots.label: BoosterPack headers
hotspots.title: 40-pin BoosterPack headers
hotspots.text: The header pins carry the chip's two ADCs, the DAC, two op-amps, four UARTs, two I2C and two SPI. Plug-on boards stack on top.

hotspots.label: LEDs
hotspots.title: Two LEDs
hotspots.text: One red, one RGB, labelled LED1 and LED2 on the silkscreen. Blinking the red one is the first project.

hotspots.label: On-board sensors
hotspots.title: Thermistor and light sensor
hotspots.text: The thermistor is marked on the board here. The light sensor is on TI's kit page list but not marked in this photo. Per TI's kit page, both are analog.
